Q: What should you define before selecting an evaluation library?
explain: Define the tasks, correct outcomes, harmful failures, and relevant constraints. Then choose measurements capable of answering those questions. A library cannot supply the product's definition of success for you.
example: A return assistant must avoid unsupported refund promises, even when the customer rates a generous answer positively.
takeaway: The rubric comes before the dashboard.

Q: Why evaluate retrieval separately from generation?
explain: Retrieval can fail to supply the necessary fact; generation can misuse a correctly supplied fact. Test both so a score change tells you where to investigate. Keep the same fixtures when comparing pipeline variants.
example: The exception is absent from top-k: retrieval failure. It is present but ignored: downstream information-use failure.

Q: How do you keep an experiment honest?
explain: Freeze the dataset and configuration for the comparison, hold back evaluation cases, and report sample sizes and failure slices. Changing several components together makes attribution difficult. Do not relabel development examples as unseen evidence.
example: Tune on one group of questions and compare final candidates on another reviewed group.
takeaway: Reproducibility requires more than saving one score.

Q: What should a failure report contain?
explain: Include the task, required fact, actual candidate evidence, final result, relevant configuration versions, and the first violated expectation. Use synthetic or approved redacted data. This makes an incident actionable without retaining unnecessary customer content.
example: The report identifies that a tenant filter removed an applicable shared article before ranking.
takeaway: A useful evaluation explains what to fix.

Q: How do retrieval metrics differ on one ranked list?
explain: Suppose relevant items are A and C, and the top three results are B, A, D. Precision@3 is 1/3 because one returned item is relevant; Recall@3 is 1/2 because one of two relevant items was found. Reciprocal rank is 1/2 because the first relevant item is at rank two. Mean reciprocal rank averages that value across queries. State whether labels refer to documents, chunks, or spans.
example: If another chunk from A appears twice, deduplicate according to the declared label unit before calculating recall. Otherwise redundant hits can inflate the apparent coverage.
takeaway: Metrics need explicit relevance units, rankings, and denominators.

Q: Which tests should run without calling a model?
explain: Test deterministic business rules, parsers, tenant boundaries, state transitions, replay, and operation uniqueness with controlled inputs. Use integration tests for real database semantics and a small end-to-end test for the user journey. Keep model evaluations in a separately budgeted suite with versioned fixtures and known variability. Mocks cannot prove database isolation or production proxy behavior.
example: A fake generator returns unsupported source IDs so the API's citation validator can be tested cheaply. A separate real integration test confirms that a task from another user cannot be read.
takeaway: Use the cheapest test that can actually expose the relevant failure.
